Next Greater Element (monotonic stack)

Keep a stack of indices whose next-greater element hasn't been found yet, with values decreasing from bottom to top. Each new value pops every smaller value off the stack, and it is the answer for each of them.
O(n), since each index is pushed and popped once

Daily Temperatures (days until a warmer day)

Monotonic decreasing stack of indices: every warmer day resolves all cooler days waiting on the stack. O(n) time, O(n) space. For a circular array (Next Greater Element II), loop i from 0 to 2n−1 and use i % n.
Largest Rectangle in Histogram

When a bar is popped, the current index is its first smaller bar on the right and the new stack top is its first smaller bar on the left, so its widest rectangle is known. O(n). "Maximal Rectangle" in a binary matrix runs this once per row on accumulated heights.
Decode String ("3[a2[c]]" → "accaccacc")
Push the count and the string built so far when entering a bracket, and pop them when leaving it. Handles nesting and multi-digit counts. O(output length) time.
Asteroid Collision
A collision only happens when the stack top moves right and the new asteroid moves left. O(n), since each asteroid is pushed and popped at most once.
Basic Calculator II ("3+2*2", no parentheses)

Apply * and / immediately to the stack top; defer + and - by pushing signed numbers and summing at the end. O(n). With parentheses (Basic Calculator I/III), push the running result and sign on (, or recurse.
Implement a Stack Using Queues

One queue is enough: after adding, rotate the older elements behind the new one so the front is always the most recent. push is O(n), pop/top O(1). In real Java code use ArrayDeque as a stack; the legacy Stack class is synchronized and extends Vector.
Car Fleet

Process cars from the front. A car that would arrive no later than the fleet ahead joins it; otherwise it starts a new fleet. This is a monotonic stack collapsed to a single value. O(n log n) for the sort.
